result.rulesSummary:
## Model

Parse args: `k1,k2` are strings (raw, no processing); `v1,v2` are **BigInt** parsed with Python `int()` grammar (optional surrounding whitespace, optional `+`/`-`, decimal digits with single `_` separators between digits; reject hex/float/exponent/empty/trailing `_`). Reject -> RC=2, empty stdout, argparse usage error on stderr.

Represent the bidict as an **ordered forward map** `string -> BigInt` (JS `Map`, never a plain object) plus an **independent inverse map** `BigInt -> string`. Keys and values are in separate namespaces: string `'999'` and BigInt `999n` never collide.

## Execution order (checks must fire in exactly this sequence)

**Step 1 — build the dict literal `{k1: v1, k2: v2}` (this happens BEFORE bidict exists).**
- If `k1 === k2`: result is a **single** entry `{k1: v2}` — **last value wins**, `v1` is silently discarded, no error. Position is index 0.
- Else: two entries in argument order `[k1->v1, k2->v2]`.

**Step 2 — `bidict(D)` construction.** Only reachable failure: `D` has 2 entries and `v1 === v2`.
- Raise, print **0 stdout lines**, RC=1, stderr:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "test19.py", line 12, in <module>
  File "bidict/_base.py", line 161, in __init__
  File "bidict/_base.py", line 454, in _update
  File "bidict/_base.py", line 347, in _dedup
bidict.ValueDuplicationError: <repr(v1)>
[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test19' due to unhandled exception!
```
(Never a KeyDuplicationError — step 1 already removed key dups.)

**Step 3 — `b2 = b1.copy()`; `print(b2)` -> stdout LINE 1.**

**Step 4 — `b1['new'] = 999`.** Let `hasNew = D.has('new')`, `owner999 = D.inverse.get(999n)` (may be undefined).
| condition | result |
|---|---|
| `hasNew && D.get('new')===999n` | **no-op**; map completely unchanged (line 2 will be byte-identical to line 1) |
| `hasNew && owner999===undefined` | **in-place value replace**: `'new'` keeps its existing POSITION (do NOT delete+reinsert) |
| `hasNew && owner999!==undefined && owner999!=='new'` | raise **KeyAndValueDuplicationError**, `_dedup` line **333**, message `('new', 999)` (constant) |
| `!hasNew && owner999!==undefined` | raise **ValueDuplicationError**, `_dedup` line **347**, message `999` (constant) |
| `!hasNew && owner999===undefined` | **append at END** |

Both raises print **exactly 1 stdout line** (line 1 only), RC=1, and share this 6-frame traceback:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "test19.py", line 17, in <module>
  File "bidict/_bidict.py", line 80, in __setitem__
  File "bidict/_bidict.py", line 106, in put
  File "bidict/_base.py", line 454, in _update
  File "bidict/_base.py", line <333|347>, in _dedup
bidict.<KeyAndValueDuplicationError: ('new', 999) | ValueDuplicationError: 999>
[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test19' due to unhandled exception!
```

**Step 5 — `print(b1)` -> LINE 2. Step 6 — `print(b2)` -> LINE 3.** Line 3 is **always byte-identical to line 1** (b2 is a deep-enough copy; clone BOTH forward and inverse maps).

**Step 7 — `b2.inv[v1]`.** Missing **iff** `k1===k2 && v1!==v2` (v1 was dropped in step 1). Then **3 stdout lines** already printed, RC=1:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "test19.py", line 22, in <module>
  File "bidict/_base.py", line 524, in __getitem__
KeyError: <repr(v1)>
[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test19' due to unhandled exception!
```
Note `KeyError` has **no** `bidict.` prefix (unlike the two bidict errors), and the key is the **dropped** v1, not the survivor.

**Step 8 — `print(result)` -> LINE 4**: the **raw** string key, no quotes/repr/escaping. RC=0.

## repr rules

`bidict({` + `, `.join(`reprStr(k) + ': ' + reprInt(v)`) + `})`. Class name is lowercase `bidict`. Empty dict is unreachable.

`reprInt`: plain decimal from BigInt, `-` for negatives, no `+`, no leading zeros, no separators, no exponent notation, arbitrary precision.

`reprStr` (Python `str.__repr__`): delimiter is `'`, unless the string contains `'` **and** no `"`, in which case the delimiter is `"` (and `'` is left unescaped). With `'` delimiter, inner `'` -> `\'`; with `"` delimiter, inner `"` -> `\"`. Always `\` -> `\\`. `\n` -> `\n`, `\r` -> `\r`, `\t` -> `\t`. Any other codepoint where Python `str.isprintable()` is false (Unicode categories Cc, Cf, Cs, Co, Cn, Zl, Zp, and Zs other than U+0020) is escaped lowercase-hex: `\xHH` for < 0x100, `\uHHHH` for BMP, `\U00HHHHHH` above. **Printable non-ASCII is emitted RAW as UTF-8** (`café`, `emoji😀`, combining U+0301 are NOT escaped). Verified escapes: U+0001->`\x01`, U+007F->`\x7f`, U+00A0->`\xa0`, U+200B->`​`, U+2028->` `.

## Unmatchable byte

`[PYI-<N>:ERROR]` — `<N>` is the executable's own **PID** (empirically BASHPID+3 across a pipe; monotonically increasing across runs). Emit `process.pid`; exact digits are unreproducible, so any differential harness must normalize this line.

result.rulesSummary:
SPEC FOR type=int ON --v1/--v2 (all empirically observed via /workspace/dataset/test19_executable)

There are TWO gates. Gate A is argparse deciding whether the token is a value at all; Gate B is Python's int() conversion. They produce DIFFERENT error messages.

=== GATE A: argparse token consumption (only applies to the space-separated form `--v1 X`) ===
Given `--v1 X` where X starts with '-':
  - If X contains a space (0x20) anywhere -> treated as a value; go to Gate B.
  - Else if X matches /^-\d+$/u OR /^-\d*\.\d+$/u (Python `re`, so \d is UNICODE Nd, e.g. -٧ and -<U+1D7FD> qualify) -> treated as a value; go to Gate B.
  - Else -> treated as an option string; argparse errors with:
        usage: test19_executable [-h] --k1 K1 --v1 V1 --k2 K2 --v2 V2\n
        test19_executable: error: argument --v1: expected one argument\n
    exit 2, empty stdout.
    Observed hits: -1_0, -5_0, -1e3, -inf, -0x10, --5.
The attached form `--v1=X` (and `--v2=X`) SKIPS Gate A entirely. So `--v1 -1_0` -> "expected one argument", but `--v1=-1_0` -> accepted as -10. This asymmetry must be modeled.
X not starting with '-' always goes to Gate B.

=== GATE B: int(X) grammar ===
1. Strip leading and trailing whitespace. The strip set observed as ACCEPTED-when-leading is exactly:
     0x09 0x0A 0x0B 0x0C 0x0D 0x20, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000, U+2001, U+2006, U+2007, U+2008, U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000.
   (U+2002-U+2005 and U+2009 were not individually probed but are in the same Zs run as the probed neighbours.)
   Observed NOT in the strip set (these cause rejection): U+FEFF, U+200B, U+200C, U+2060, U+180E, U+00AD, and 0x1C 0x1D 0x1E 0x1F.
   => Do NOT use JS String.prototype.trim(): it strips U+FEFF (Python does not) and omits U+0085 (Python strips it). Use the explicit list.
2. After stripping, the remainder must match:
       ( '+' | '-' )?  D  ( '_'? D )*
   where D is a single character of Unicode general category Nd (any script, any plane), and there is at least one D.
   - Sign must be ASCII 0x2B/0x2D only (U+2212, U+FF0B rejected), at most one, immediately before the first digit (no whitespace allowed between sign and digit: '+ 5', '- 5', '-\t5' all rejected).
   - Underscores: single only, strictly between two digits. Rejected: _1, 1_, 1__0, +_1.
   - Nd digits from different scripts/planes may be mixed freely: '7٧'->77, '1<U+1D7FD>'->17, '٧_٨'->78, '<U+1D7FD><U+1D7F6>'->70.
   - Digit value is the character's decimal value (U+0660->0 ... U+0669->9, U+FF10..19, U+1D7CE.., U+1D7F6.., U+104A0.., U+0966.., U+09E6.., U+0E50.., U+1810..).
   - Categories No and Nl are NOT digits: ² (U+00B2) and Ⅷ (U+2167) rejected.
   - Leading zeros allowed and meaningless (decimal, never octal): 007->7, -007->-7, '0'*4300 -> 0.
3. DIGIT-COUNT LIMIT: if the number of Nd characters (excluding sign and underscores, INCLUDING leading zeros) exceeds 4300, reject. Verified boundary: 4300 digits accept, 4301 reject; '0'*4300 accept, '0'*4301 reject; '0'+'1'*4300 reject; 4300 digits with 1433 underscores accept (strlen 5733); 4301 digits with underscores reject; '-' + 4300 digits accept, '-' + 4301 digits reject. The error message is the ORDINARY invalid-int message with the whole original string echoed (no special "too large" wording).
4. Value is an arbitrary-precision integer. Must be BigInt in JS. 40-digit and 2**53+1 inputs are echoed digit-exact in the bidict repr (9007199254740993 stays ...993). Print with plain decimal, no exponent, no 'n' suffix. -0 prints as 0.

=== REJECTION OUTPUT (Gate B failure) ===
Two lines to stderr, nothing to stdout, exit code 2:
  line1: "usage: test19_executable [-h] --k1 K1 --v1 V1 --k2 K2 --v2 V2\n"   (61 chars + LF)
  line2: "test19_executable: error: argument " + FLAG + ": invalid int value: " + REPR + "\n"
FLAG is "--v1" or "--v2". The prefix "test19_executable: error: argument --v1: invalid int value: " is exactly 60 bytes.
REPR is Python repr() of the ORIGINAL, UNSTRIPPED value string:
  - Quote choice: default single quotes. If the string contains ' and does NOT contain " -> use double quotes and leave ' unescaped ("it's"). If it contains BOTH -> single quotes with \' escaped and " literal ('it\'s a "x"').
  - Backslash -> \\ .
  - 0x0A -> \n, 0x0D -> \r, 0x09 -> \t (as two literal ASCII bytes, so stderr stays one physical line).
  - Other non-printables: \xNN for code points < 0x100 (U+00AD -> \xad, 0x01 -> \x01, 0x1C -> \x1c), \uNNNN for BMP (U+FEFF -> ﻿, U+200B -> ​, U+180E -> ᠎, U+2060 -> ⁠). Lowercase hex.
  - Printable non-ASCII passes through as RAW UTF-8, unescaped (² -> bytes c2 b2; ＋ -> ef bc 8b; − -> e2 88 92; '٧ ٨' -> d9 a7 20 d9 a8).
  - Undecodable argv bytes (PEP 383 surrogateescape): byte 0xFF -> \udcff. Node must read raw argv bytes to reproduce this, not the lossy U+FFFD decode.

Only the FIRST failure in COMMAND-LINE order is reported. `--v1 xx --v2 yy` reports --v1; `--v2 yy --v1 xx` reports --v2. A type-conversion failure also pre-empts the "required argument missing" error (`--k1 a --v1 xx --v2 2` reports the --v1 int error, not missing --k2).

result.rulesSummary:
STREAM ROUTING
- All four `print()` outputs go to STDOUT, each terminated by exactly one LF (0x0A). Never CR, never CRLF (any \r\n seen in probes came from the pty's ONLCR, not the program). The final stdout line IS newline-terminated and there is no extra trailing blank line. Success stdout for `--k1 a --v1 1 --k2 b --v2 2` is exactly 89 bytes.
- Python tracebacks go to STDERR. PyInstaller then appends one more STDERR line: `[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test19' due to unhandled exception!\n`, always LAST of the program-exception block.
- argparse `--help` goes to STDOUT (158 bytes, exit 0). argparse errors go to STDERR (usage line + `<prog>: error: ...` line, exit 2, stdout exactly 0 bytes).
- `<prog>` = basename(argv[0]); verified `renamed_prog` via symlink.

EXIT CODES (complete observed set)
- 0 : normal completion; also `--help`; also `| head -3`/`head -4` early-close of a large stdout; also stdout-flush ENOSPC at normal exit; also fd1 closed with `>&-`.
- 1 : any uncaught Python exception, including BrokenPipeError. NEVER 141 — SIGPIPE does not kill the process.
- 2 : any argparse error (missing required, bad int, unrecognized arguments).
- 120 : `--help` when the stdout flush fails (`--help >/dev/full`). Deterministic.
- Exit 0 with NON-EMPTY stderr is reachable (the `| head -3` and `>/dev/full` success cases). Do not couple stderr-nonempty to nonzero exit.

BUFFERING MODEL (the core of this dimension) — reproduce exactly:
- STDERR: effectively unbuffered; every stderr byte hits the fd before the program continues.
- STDOUT when `isTTY` is TRUE: line-buffered. Flush on each `\n`. Result: stdout lines appear BEFORE any traceback.
- STDOUT when `isTTY` is FALSE (pipe OR regular file OR /dev/null — behaviour is identical for all): block-buffered with a buffer of EXACTLY 8192 bytes. Pending stdout is flushed only when the buffer reaches 8192 bytes, or at interpreter exit — which happens AFTER all stderr output including the `[PYI-...]` line. Result: in a merged stream (`2>&1 | cat` or `>file 2>&1`) the FULL traceback + PYI line appear BEFORE the buffered stdout lines, which then follow in their original relative order.
- Implement `print(x)` as TWO writes into that buffer: `write(repr(x))` then `write("\n")`. This is observable: with a repr of 8195 bytes the repr is flushed straight through (ending `...2})` with NO newline), the traceback is written, and the orphan `\n` is flushed at exit — the merged file literally contains `2})Traceback (most recent call last):` and ends `exception!\n\n`. Measured flip point is exact: 8191 pending bytes stay buffered, 8192 triggers the flush (K=8165 -> traceback first; K=8166 -> stdout first with Traceback at byte offset 8192).
- ENV VARS ARE IGNORED: `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1`, `stdbuf -o0`, `PYTHONIOENCODING=ascii|latin-1`, `LC_ALL=C`, `LANG=C`, `PYTHONVERBOSE=1` all produce byte-identical output. stdout encoding is fixed UTF-8, raw, no BOM, no escaping.

EARLY-CLOSED / UNWRITABLE STDOUT
- Small output + `| head -1`: no error at all, exit 0, stderr empty (the whole 89-byte buffer fits one pipe write).
- Output > 64KB pipe capacity + early close: `BrokenPipeError: [Errno 32] Broken pipe`, exit 1. The traceback's `test19.py` line number identifies which print failed — this maps the source: print#1=line 14, print#2=line 18, print#3=line 19, print#4=line 23; and `b1['new']=999`=line 17, `bidict({...})` construction=line 12, `b2.inv[args.v1]`=line 22.
- If bytes remain in the 8192 buffer at exit, a SECOND stderr block follows the PYI line:
  `Traceback (most recent call last):\n  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>\n<ERR>\nException ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper name='<stdout>' mode='w' encoding='utf-8'>\n<ERR>\n`
  where `<ERR>` is `BrokenPipeError: [Errno 32] Broken pipe` or `OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device`. Note the unusual order: the Traceback lines come BEFORE the `Exception ignored in:` header. If the buffer was already drained (e.g. EPIPE during print#1), this block is ABSENT.
- `--help >/dev/full` emits ONLY the 2-line `Exception ignored in: ...` / `OSError: [Errno 28] ...` block (128 bytes) and exits 120.
- `>&-` (fd1 closed) -> exit 0 and stderr `Traceback (most recent call last):\n  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>\nAttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'flush'\n`.
- `2>&-` -> exit code unaffected (still 1); traceback simply discarded.

NON-DETERMINISM (exhaustive)
- The ONLY bytes that vary across runs are the decimal digits `<N>` in `[PYI-<N>:ERROR]`. 8 repeats of the same failing probe diffed to exactly `8c8`; 5 repeats of the broken-pipe probe diffed to exactly `4c4`. `<N>` is the process PID: plain decimal, no zero padding, variable width (observed 655 … 2886, tracking the shell's `$$` a few above). Everything else — every traceback line, every frame, every byte count — is stable. The `/dev/full` and `--help >/dev/full` stderr blocks contain no PID and are 100% byte-stable.
- A JS port must print its real `process.pid` there; a byte-diff harness must mask `/PYI-[0-9]+/`.

DISTINCT STDERR TEMPLATES (byte counts with a 3-digit pid)
- ValueDuplicationError at line 17 (dup value vs 999): 379 B, frames test19.py:17, bidict/_bidict.py:80 __setitem__, bidict/_bidict.py:106 put, bidict/_base.py:454 _update, bidict/_base.py:347 _dedup; final `bidict.ValueDuplicationError: <v>`.
- KeyAndValueDuplicationError at line 17 (k=='new' and v==999): 394 B, same frames but `_dedup` at line 333; final `bidict.KeyAndValueDuplicationError: ('new', 999)`.
- ValueDuplicationError at line 12 (construction, v1==v2): 328 B, frames test19.py:12, bidict/_base.py:161 __init__, :454 _update, :347 _dedup. stdout 0 bytes.
- KeyError at line 22 (k1==k2): 218 B, frames test19.py:22, bidict/_base.py:524 __getitem__; final `KeyError: <v1>`. stdout 63 bytes (3 lines).
- BrokenPipeError: frames just `test19.py:<print line>`; final `BrokenPipeError: [Errno 32] Broken pipe`.
No `File` line is ever followed by a source-code line — this PyInstaller build ships no .py sources, so the traceback is frame lines only.

Unicode 16.0 Nd digits are REJECTED by int(): `--v1 <U+10D41>` (printf '\xf0\x90\xb5\x81') -> RC=2; same for U+116D1, U+1E5F1, U+1CCF1. Unicode 15.0 digits are accepted: `--v1 <U+11F51>` -> `bidict({'a': 1, ...})`, U+1E4F1 -> 1. Printability: Unicode 15.1 additions are treated as UNASSIGNED and escaped — `--k1 <U+2FFC>` -> `bidict({'⿼': 1, ...})`, U+31EF -> `'㇯'`, U+2EBF0 -> `'\U0002ebf0'`, U+2EE5D -> `'\U0002ee5d'`; Unicode 16.0 additions likewise escaped (U+10D40 -> `'\U00010d40'`, U+16D40, U+105C0, U+1CC00, U+1E5D0). On Node 23+ `\p{Nd}` matches U+10D41 and `\p{Cn}` does not match U+2FFC, so a category-based port diverges on both the int grammar and the escaping.

Surrogate-pair handling in a UTF-16 port: astral printables are emitted RAW (`--k1 <U+1F600>` -> `bidict({'😀': 1, ...})`) and astral non-printables use `\U00hhhhhh` with 8 lowercase hex digits (`--k1 <U+100000>` -> `'\U00100000'`). A JS port iterating UTF-16 code units would test each surrogate half (both Cs -> escaped) and produce `😀`. Confirm the port iterates by code point: `printf '\xf0\x9f\x98\x80' | xargs -0 -I{} /workspace/dataset/test19_executable --k1 {} --v1 1 --k2 zz --v2 2 | head -1 | od -An -tx1` (expect `27 f0 9f 98 80 27`). Also probe a PAIRED lone-surrogate spelled via argv bytes vs a real astral char to be sure the port distinguishes real surrogates (`\udcff` from surrogateescape) from surrogate pairs.

Insertion-order wording: the spec says the two entries are "in argument order [k1->v1, k2->v2]". I verified order is SOURCE order (k1 first) and is completely independent of command-line order: `/workspace/dataset/test19_executable --v2 2 --k2 b --v1 1 --k1 a` -> `bidict({'a': 1, 'b': 2})` (identical to the canonical order). Reword to "k1 entry first, then k2, regardless of CLI order" so a port does not try to track CLI positions. Also pin repeated-option semantics, which the spec omits: last occurrence wins (`--k1 a --k1 z ...` -> `bidict({'z': 1, ...})`; `--v1 1 --v1 5` -> 5).
